PullRequest.Title: transitioning to clipboard api
PullRequest.Body:

Related issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/252371

## Summary

Adds an opt-in Async Clipboard API implementation for editor cut, copy, and paste, controlled by `editor.experimentalClipboardApi`. The setting defaults to `false`, retaining the existing clipboard execution paths unless explicitly enabled.

## Implementation

- Adds shared rich clipboard operations to the browser and desktop clipboard services, supporting text, HTML, images, and custom formats.
- Converts between browser clipboard data and VS Code's data-transfer representation. Custom formats use the required `web ` prefix when written and are normalized when read.
- Routes rich paste data through existing paste providers before applying the default text paste.
- Exposes the experimental option through the standalone editor configuration and Monaco declarations.

## Verification with debugger

It has been verified with the debugger that the new code paths are being hit when doing copy pasting

## Manual Verification Checklist

In the following unless states otherwise have `editor.experimentalClipboardApi` enabled.

### Configuration and Basic Operations

- [x] With the setting disabled, verify existing cut, copy, and paste behavior remains unchanged.
- [x] Enable `editor.experimentalClipboardApi`, confirm with the debugger that the new code is hit.
- [x] Disable the setting without restarting and verify commands use the legacy code with the debugger. 
- [x] Copy and cut selected text, then paste into another editor and an external application. Verify the copied text and cut range are correct.
- [x] Verify undo/redo for cut and paste.

### Metadata and Rich Formats

- [x] Copy without a selection with `editor.emptySelectionClipboard` enabled and disabled; verify whole-line is copied if setting is turned on.
- [x] Copy multiple selections and paste into matching cursors; verify each selection receives the correct text.
- [x] Verify block-selection copy/paste and copy between editor windows.
- [x] Exercise **Paste As**, for example on pasting links in markdown file, and verify the paste as widget appears and can be used
- [x] Paste a screenshot into Markdown with an applicable image-paste provider; verify the image file and inserted reference.
  - Open a saved .md file in the source editor, with language mode Markdown.
  - Press Control+Shift+Command+4, then select a screen region. This copies the screenshot to the clipboard.
  - Place the cursor on a blank line outside a code block and press Command+V.
  - If needed, use Paste As… → Insert Markdown Image.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The allocation, call path, and before/after behavior are directly visible: all API pastes await this loop before firing providers, file.data() performs blob.arrayBuffer(), and the existing provider bridge demonstrably preserves file.data() as a lazy resolver. Only the exact browser-level copy count and payload sizes vary.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Binary clipboard bytes allocated as an ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array and copied again into a new Uint8Array and File for every file representation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The transient allocation and decoding cost grows with the summed size of all binary clipboard representations; a single high-resolution screenshot can be many megabytes, and multiple representations are processed sequentially before paste can proceed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased paste latency plus transient memory and GC pressure on image/media paste
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The legacy paste route received browser-owned File objects from the ClipboardEvent and converted them to VSDataTransfer items whose data() callback read bytes only when a provider requested them; the extension-host DataTransferFileCache likewise resolves file bytes lazily.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The experimental Clipboard API route first creates lazy file items in readClipboardData, then calls toDataTransfer before firing onWillPaste; this added line eagerly awaits every file.data(), allocates another Uint8Array, and constructs a new File before providers are selected or invoked.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added file branch at RIGHT line 17 (`new File([new Uint8Array(await file.data())], ...)`) is the new eager byte-materialization step, and the same PR adds its unconditional invocation on the experimental paste critical path at src/vs/editor/contrib/clipboard/browser/clipboard.ts:461.
Findings.Title: Keep clipboard files lazy until a paste provider requests them
Findings.Impact: With editor.experimentalClipboardApi enabled, pasting a screenshot or other large media blocks provider dispatch on full payload materialization and creates multiple payload-sized transient allocations, causing slower paste and avoidable GC/memory spikes even when no provider ultimately consumes that file.
Findings.Evidence: readClipboardData stores non-text blobs behind a lazy data() callback (src/vs/base/browser/clipboard.ts:46), but executeClipboardApiPaste unconditionally awaits toDataTransfer before triggerOnWillPaste (src/vs/editor/contrib/clipboard/browser/clipboard.ts:461-463). This line calls file.data(), wraps the returned Uint8Array in a new Uint8Array, and then a File. Existing paste providers consume VSDataTransfer; DataTransferFileCache.resolveFileData invokes file.data() only on demand, and the Markdown image provider carries DataTransferFile contents into its workspace edit without eagerly calling data().
Findings.Recommendation: Avoid round-tripping the Clipboard API result through a DOM DataTransfer. Build the paste event directly over the IReadonlyVSDataTransfer: parse only text/metadata eagerly, expose file names/types without reading bytes, and return the original lazy transfer to paste providers so file.data() runs only for the selected provider.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor copy or cut with editor.experimentalClipboardApi enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection/text/HTML generation and synchronous onWillCopy/onWillCut hooks precede a single awaited navigator.clipboard.write; a cut mutates the model only after that write succeeds. Provider prepareDocumentPaste operations launched by CopyPasteController remain off the clipboard-write critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser/OS rich clipboard write containing all MIME representations in one ClipboardItem
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser clipboard write per copy/cut command; format payloads are grouped into that one write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor command used execCommand('copy'/'cut') and a ClipboardEvent, with a native text-only fallback for an Electron failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits completion; cut waits before deleting selected text.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing document paste providers prepare copy metadata/data in extension hosts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one operation per applicable prepare-paste provider for the logical copy; provider count is normally small.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same onWillCopy/onWillCut hook started these provider operations on the legacy clipboard-event route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Operations are started by the synchronous hook but are not awaited by the Clipboard API write; prepared data is merged later on paste.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected text size, number of MIME formats contributed by hooks, and number of existing prepare-paste providers; effective clipboard boundary cardinality remains one write per command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Clipboard API write is awaited per command. Existing prepare-paste providers may start concurrently by provider, but this behavior already ran from the legacy onWillCopy/onWillCut event and is not introduced or amplified.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No clipboard write cache or coalescing is used. In-memory editor metadata is a single last-copy entry and does not retain payload bytes; cold and repeated writes each serialize the current selection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the command and service call graph shows one grouped write and unchanged provider preparation ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Clipboard write duration and extension/provider count vary by browser and installed extensions, but no new per-item boundary fan-out is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new opt-in implementation necessarily serializes selected data but batches formats into one clipboard boundary and does not add scaling boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Plain-text and rich-text editor paste with the experimental API enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single navigator.clipboard.read completes, each available string representation is decoded, the result is converted for the editor event, synchronous onWillPaste listeners run, and either an existing paste provider operation or the default text paste completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser/OS rich clipboard read and per-format Blob retrieval
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard.read per paste and one getType per advertised representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The browser supplied DataTransfer through a ClipboardEvent triggered by the legacy paste route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads and text decoding complete before editor paste listeners or default insertion can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing paste-edit provider invocation in extension hosts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per matching provider, using one data-transfer DTO per request; provider count is bounded by registered applicable providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same CopyPasteController provider dispatch ran for legacy ClipboardEvent paste data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only applies when paste providers are enabled and match the clipboard types; default text paste otherwise proceeds without this IPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and total size of clipboard text/custom formats plus applicable paste-provider count; common clipboard contents have a few representations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Clipboard items and formats are read sequentially by the new loops. Existing applicable providers may be queried concurrently downstream; no added unbounded task launch was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No clipboard read cache or in-flight coalescing is used, so each paste sees current clipboard contents. Provider copy metadata can reference existing prepared data; this does not cache clipboard payload decoding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-read/per-format critical path; low evidence of harmful magnitude for ordinary text formats.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom-format count and Blob decoding cost vary, but typical text clipboard cardinality is low and no evidence establishes a material regression independent of the intended rich read.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The read is a required part of the opted-in rich API path, typical effective cardinality is small, and no avoidable boundary fan-out was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pasting a screenshot or other binary media into an editor with the experimental API enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser clipboard read yields lazy VSDataTransfer file items, but toDataTransfer then awaits every file.data(), allocates another Uint8Array and File sequentially, and only afterward fires onWillPaste. Matching paste providers then run and may save the selected media through an existing workspace edit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser/OS rich clipboard read and binary Blob retrieval
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard.read per paste and one getType per advertised image/media representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy ClipboardEvent paste supplied browser-owned File objects directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before conversion and provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full Blob-to-ArrayBuffer conversion followed by Uint8Array and File construction for every binary item
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per binary transfer entry, with bytes proportional to that entry's full payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy conversion wrapped File.arrayBuffer behind IDataTransferFile.data(); providers and the extension-host file cache requested bytes lazily.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All payload materialization and copies complete before onWillPaste and before provider filtering/consumption.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Matching paste-provider request and optional lazy file-data resolution to an extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request per matching provider; at most one file-data resolution per file actually requested by that provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing legacy paste providers received lazy file items and resolved bytes on demand.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider selection/edit computation occurs after the newly eager conversion; file-data IPC is only incurred when provider logic or an applied edit needs bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/write pasted media file through the provider's workspace edit
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one create/write for one pasted screenshot; scales with accepted media files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Markdown provider already created workspace media files for legacy image paste.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs only after a matching provider creates and the editor applies the paste edit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Summed bytes across all binary clipboard representations, number of binary representations, and matching providers/files. A realistic high-resolution screenshot is a single multi-megabyte image; multiple advertised media representations increase the total proportionally.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Binary materialization is serialized across transfer entries before provider dispatch. Existing matching providers can run downstream; the eager allocations cannot overlap with or be skipped based on provider selection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Clipboard API service initially exposes each Blob through a lazy data() callback, with no byte cache. The new conversion consumes every callback once before dispatch; the existing extension-host bridge otherwise resolves only a requested file and does not require warm-cache materialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence: the new command unconditionally awaits toDataTransfer, the added file branch explicitly calls lazy file.data(), and the existing provider bridge proves bytes can remain lazy.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact screenshot compression, browser Blob/File internal copy behavior, and GC timing vary, but blob.arrayBuffer plus the explicit new Uint8Array guarantee payload-sized work before provider dispatch.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium performance regression. The diff defeats lazy binary ownership and adds full-payload critical-path allocations before knowing whether a provider will consume the media.

Scenarios.Scenario: Legacy clipboard routes and Safari text-write workaround
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With the option disabled, existing editor execCommand/triggerPaste routes remain selected. On Safari text writes, a user-gesture-started clipboard.write now has its result awaited after pending text is supplied; fallback execCommand creates and removes one textarea.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pending browser write per gesture and one acknowledgement awaited by the corresponding writeText.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The browser write itself already started on every relevant gesture; the diff records and awaits its existing result rather than adding another write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: writeText now resolves with the actual browser write result instead of only completing the supplied-data promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One text payload and one clipboard operation per command; cost scales with text length but not collection cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Safari workaround retains only the latest pending user-gesture write and cancels an unresolved predecessor's data promise. One write result is awaited by the matching writeText call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No payload cache. Pending state is cleared when consumed or replaced, so no unbounded retention was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: changed state tracks the already-existing clipboard.write promise and introduces no additional browser call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser acknowledgement latency varies, but boundary count and payload work are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Waiting for the existing acknowledgement is bounded to one operation and does not add work, fan-out, or retention; the default editor route remains legacy unless explicitly enabled.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 18 changed files and traced experimental editor copy, cut, text/rich paste, image paste, legacy fallback, and Safari write acknowledgement paths. One medium eager-allocation regression was reported: the new image paste route defeats lazy file data and creates payload-sized copies before providers run. Clipboard boundary cardinality is otherwise bounded and existing provider/IPC/filesystem work is not amplified by the diff.
